picks.file: Anverpia from Braun and Hogenberg's Civitates Orbis Terrarum MET DP325824.jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1 (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
picks.why: clean colored copy; walled city on the Scheldt with the cathedral and the new citadel; sheet margins cut

picks.file: Gezicht op Antwerpen Antwerpen (titel op object), RP-P-AO-17-24A.jpg
picks.what: View from the Scheldt, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Circuli Burgundici
picks.why: river panorama with the cathedral spire; cleaner sheet than #9 (same plate, Plantin-Moretus dates it 1651)

picks.file: Egide Linnig - Panoramic view of the city and the wharf of Antwerp from the left bank.jpg
picks.what: The city and the riverfront from the left bank, panoramic lithograph
picks.why: general river view with the cathedral; very long strip trimmed to its central half around the cathedral, title and labels cut

picks.what: Antwerp across the Scheldt, photochrom print
picks.why: classic color river view with the cathedral tower and the Steen; cleaned copy of #25

picks.file: American First World War Official Exchange Collection Q64696.jpg
picks.what: General view over the roofs to the Scheldt, photograph (U.S. Army Signal Corps)
picks.why: firmly dated high view of the old town, St. Paul’s Church and the river; trim cuts the negative number

picks.what: The cathedral and the Boerentoren from the left bank, photograph
picks.why: sharp modern skyline across the Scheldt; echoes the 1654 and 1890s views

notes: P3 second view possible: #20 Samuel Ireland aquatint ‘Antwerp from across the Scheld’ (record says 1795, but his tour book first appeared 1790; small plate), left out for the date doubt. Skipped siege prints (#16–19) and the 1940–50 aerial (#29, vague date).
